title: Energy, Power and Efficiency
description: KE, GPE, P=IV, efficiency — the workhorse physics calculations.

method_card.title: Energy, Power and Efficiency
method_card.content:
These are the most frequently tested physics calculations. Learn each equation and its rearrangements cold.

Recall equations (must memorise):

  • \(E_k = \tfrac{1}{2}mv^2\) — kinetic energy (J) = ½ × mass (kg) × speed² (m/s)²
  • \(E_p = mgh\) — gravitational PE (J) = mass (kg) × g (N/kg) × height (m)
  • \(P = \dfrac{E}{t}\) — power (W) = energy (J) ÷ time (s)
  • \(P = IV\) — electrical power (W) = current (A) × potential difference (V)
  • \(P = I^2R\) — power using resistance
  • \(\text{efficiency} = \dfrac{\text{useful output energy}}{\text{total input energy}}\) — express as a decimal or percentage

Use g = 9.8 N/kg unless the question specifies otherwise.

Common errors:

  • For KE: always square the speed first, then multiply by ½ and mass. Forgetting to square is the most common single error in Physics exams.
  • Efficiency must be between 0 and 1 (or 0% and 100%). If you get above 1, you have divided the wrong way round.
  • For P = IV, current is in amperes and pd is in volts — check both before substituting.
steps: Identify the equation needed from the quantities given in the question
Check units: mass in kg, speed in m/s, height in m, energy in J, power in W
For KE: square the speed first, then multiply by ½ and mass
For efficiency: useful ÷ total (result between 0 and 1, or multiply by 100 for %)
State the answer with the correct unit

exam_context.marks: 2–5 marks per calculation; efficiency may include a follow-up on energy wasted as heat
exam_context.frequency: Very high — energy and power calculations appear in virtually every Physics paper

worked_examples.question: A 600 kg car travels at 20 m/s. Calculate its kinetic energy.
A pump lifts 200 kg of water through a height of 5.0 m in 10 s. Calculate the useful power output. (g = 9.8 N/kg)

steps.label: Step 1 — Calculate the work done against gravity (= GPE gained)

worked_examples.question: A motor has an input power of 500 W and lifts a 10 kg mass 8.0 m in 4.0 s. (g = 9.8 N/kg) Calculate (a) the useful output power and (b) the efficiency.

steps.label: Step 1 — Calculate useful energy output (GPE gained)

bronze.display: Calculate the kinetic energy of a 1200 kg car travelling at 30 m/s.

misconceptions.message: v² = 30² = 900. Eₖ = 0.5 × 1200 × 900 = 540 000 J. Don't multiply by 30 without squaring first.
Remember the ½ in Eₖ = ½mv².

bronze.display: A 50 kg cyclist rides at 10 m/s. Calculate their kinetic energy.

misconceptions.message: Eₖ = ½ × 50 × 100 = 2500 J. The ½ halves the answer.

bronze.display: Calculate the gravitational PE of a 5.0 kg object raised 3.0 m above the ground. (g = 9.8 N/kg)

misconceptions.message: Ep = 5.0 × 9.8 × 3.0 = 147 J. All three values must be multiplied together.

bronze.display: An electric heater transfers 9000 J of energy in 3 minutes. Calculate the power output in watts.
bronze.equation_hint: \(P = E \div t\). Convert minutes to seconds first.

misconceptions.message: 3 minutes = 180 s. P = 9000 ÷ 180 = 50 W. Always convert time to seconds.

bronze.display: A lamp operates at 12 V and draws a current of 2.5 A. Calculate its power.

misconceptions.message: P = IV = 2.5 × 12 = 30 W. Don't divide — multiply current by voltage.

bronze.display: A machine has an input of 5000 J and a useful output of 3500 J. Calculate the efficiency as a decimal.

misconceptions.message: Efficiency = 3500 ÷ 5000 = 0.7. Don't divide input by output.
Efficiency is always useful ÷ total. The answer should be between 0 and 1.

bronze.display: A kettle has a power rating of 2000 W. How much energy does it transfer in 90 s?
bronze.equation_hint: Rearrange \(P = E \div t\) to find \(E = P \times t\)

bronze.display: A motor uses a current of 5 A at a potential difference of 240 V. Calculate its power.

silver.display: A 0.5 kg ball is thrown upward and reaches a height of 10 m above the release point. Calculate the increase in gravitational PE. (g = 9.8 N/kg)
A 2.0 kg object slides down a frictionless slope and falls a vertical height of 5.0 m. Assuming all GPE converts to KE, calculate the speed at the bottom. (g = 9.8 N/kg)
silver.equation_hint: GPE lost = KE gained. Set \(mgh = \tfrac{1}{2}mv^2\), masses cancel, rearrange for v.

misconceptions.message: mgh = ½mv² → v² = 2gh = 2×9.8×5 = 98 → v = √98 = 9.9 m/s. Remember to square-root.
v² = 2gh (the 2 comes from the ½ in ½mv²). v = √(2×9.8×5) = 9.9 m/s.

silver.display: An electric motor has an input power of 800 W and efficiency of 0.75. Calculate the useful power output.
silver.equation_hint: Rearrange efficiency formula: useful output = efficiency × total input

misconceptions.message: Useful output = efficiency × input = 0.75 × 800 = 600 W. Don't divide.

silver.display: A resistor with resistance 20 Ω carries a current of 3.0 A. Calculate the power dissipated.

misconceptions.message: P = I²R = 3.0² × 20 = 9 × 20 = 180 W. Square the current first.
Use P = I²R when you have current and resistance. P = 9 × 20 = 180 W.

silver.display: A car's engine provides 45 000 J of energy. Only 36 000 J does useful work. Calculate the percentage efficiency.
A phone charger draws 0.5 A at 5.0 V. How much energy does it transfer in 2 hours?
silver.equation_hint: First find power: \(P = IV\), then energy: \(E = Pt\) (convert hours to seconds).

misconceptions.message: Always convert hours to seconds: 2 hours = 7200 s.

gold.display: A 1500 kg car travelling at 25 m/s brakes to rest. All kinetic energy is converted to thermal energy in the brakes. Calculate the temperature rise of the 15 kg steel brake discs. (Specific heat capacity of steel = 500 J/kg°C)

misconceptions.message: KE = ½mv² = 0.5×1500×625 = 468750 J. Then use ΔE = mcΔθ rearranged: Δθ = ΔE÷(mc) = 468750÷7500 = 62.5°C.

gold.display: A generator produces 230 V and has an internal resistance of 2.0 Ω. If the current is 10 A, calculate (a) the electrical power output to the external circuit and (b) the power wasted internally.

misconceptions.message: Output power P = IV = 10 × 230 = 2300 W. Internal power = I²R = 10² × 2.0 = 200 W.
Output: P = IV = 2300 W. Internal waste: P = I²R = 100 × 2.0 = 200 W.

gold.display: A wind turbine produces 5.0 MW of electrical power. The wind supplies 12 MW to the blades. Calculate the efficiency and the power wasted.

misconceptions.message: Efficiency = useful ÷ total = 5.0÷12 = 0.417. Power wasted = 12 − 5 = 7 MW.
Efficiency = 5.0÷12 = 0.417 (41.7%). Never exceed 1 (100%).

gold.display: A 70 kg person runs up a flight of stairs (vertical height 5.0 m) in 4.0 s. Calculate their useful power output. (g = 9.8 N/kg)

misconceptions.message: Find GPE gained first (mgh), then divide by time to get power.

gold.display: A ball of mass 0.4 kg is dropped from a height of 20 m. It bounces back to 12 m. Calculate the energy lost on impact. (g = 9.8 N/kg)

misconceptions.message: Calculate initial and final GPE separately, then subtract.

gold.display: A mains appliance (230 V) has a power rating of 1150 W. Calculate the current drawn and the resistance. Give resistance to 3 significant figures.

misconceptions.message: First I = P÷V = 5.0 A, then R = V÷I = 46.0 Ω.
